---
name: factory-commit
description: Turn the working tree into small Conventional Commits that pass the repo's git hooks, showing the plan and asking before committing. Use when a feature or fix is ready to commit.
argument-hint: "[--all-in-one] [extra context for the message]"
---

<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.17.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Commit the current work. Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

1. **Preconditions**: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. If it is a shared branch (see
   `.claude/skills/factory-checkout-branch/SKILL.md`, step 1: protected branches
   `main,master,develop,staging`, the origin default, `CLAUDE.md` targets, CI push branches),
   stop and suggest `/factory-checkout-branch` first.
2. **Read the change**: `git status --porcelain`, `git diff`, `git diff --cached`. Never stage
   `.env*` (except `.env.example`), credentials, large binaries, or build output; if such a file
   shows up, list it and leave it out.
3. **Conventions**: look for commitlint config (`commitlint.config.*`, `.commitlintrc*`), a
   `CLAUDE.md` commit rule, and `git log --oneline -15` for the house style (scopes, casing,
   ticket references, trailers). Default is Conventional Commits: `type(scope): subject`,
   imperative mood, lower-case subject, no trailing period, ≤ 72 characters, body explains *why*.
   Add the attribution trailer only if `CLAUDE.md` or the session asks for one.
4. **Plan the commits**: group the changes into the smallest set of commits that each make sense on
   their own (for example the feature, its tests, a drive-by refactor, docs). Tests go with the
   code they test unless the repo does otherwise. `--all-in-one` makes a single commit. If a file
   mixes unrelated changes, keep it whole in the more relevant commit rather than splitting hunks.
5. **Show and ask**: list each planned commit with its files and full message. Ask "Commit these?"
   and commit only on a clear yes. Apply any edits the user asks for.
6. **Commit**: for each commit, `git add <files>` then `git commit -m <subject> -m <body>`. Never use
   `--no-verify`, `--amend` on pushed commits, or `git add -A` blindly.
   If a hook fails (lint-staged, commitlint, tests), read its output, fix the cause, re-stage, and
   create the commit again. Do not amend the previous commit to recover.
7. **Report**: `git log --oneline origin/<base>..HEAD` (or the last N commits) and a clean
   `git status`.
